findings.message: The dev latency setting's actual behaviour has no test. apps/web/src/duel.test.ts:47-54 only checks devLatencyFromQuery's query parsing, and scripts/smoke-build.ts:77-87 only checks that the production bundle lacks the marker string. No unit, integration or browser test runs applyDevLatency / DelayLine (apps/web/src/devLatency.ts:26-61) to show that outgoing and incoming messages (probes included) are delayed by about rtt/2 each way, that jitter is added, or that order is kept. No e2e spec loads the page with ?rtt=&jitter=. Nothing checks that the reported RTT or the chosen input delay rises under the setting. The operator's playtest at §19 latencies depends on this setting working.
findings.requirement: delays the client's socket in both directions, round-trip probes included, and adds jitter

findings.message: No test checks that input delay selection follows the measured latency. The only live assertion is the local case (tests/integration/duel.test.ts:141-147: delay === MIN_INPUT_DELAY, plus at least 20 RTT samples). In the harness at 80 ms / 20 ms / 1 % (tests/integration/duelHarness.test.ts:122, 158-163), diagnostics.inputDelay is only annotated and printed; expectWithinBudget never checks it. So nothing asserts that the countdown probes measure the proxied round trip or that the room picks a delay above the minimum from it. The summary's 'input delay 3 and 7' is unchecked output. chooseInputDelay and linkStats are unit-tested in isolation only (packages/simulation/src/netcode/netcode.test.ts:97-111).
findings.requirement: chosen once per duel from round-trip and jitter measured during the countdown, applied to both players, and shown in the HUD

findings.message: No test checks the HUD's stamina display. apps/web/src/duelHud.ts:81-83 renders duel-stamina-<player> (data-value and --fill), but neither tests/e2e/duel.spec.ts nor apps/web/src/duel.test.ts reads it. Health bars, the clock, the connection line and the result are all asserted. Stamina is checked only on the server state (tests/integration/duel.test.ts:207), not on what the HUD shows.
findings.requirement: A duel HUD (§13) shows both health bars, stamina, the round clock, the connection line (round-trip, input delay, corrections) and the result screen.

findings.message: The resync-after-stall test (packages/simulation/src/netcode/netcode.test.ts:410-423) asserts only session.frame and the resyncs counter; its last assertion, expect(bundle).toBeDefined(), checks nothing. It never checks that the session's confirmed or predicted state was restored from the latest snapshot (for example hashState(session.confirmedState) === hashState(authority.state)). The snapshot is also delivered as a frame gap, so applyBundle has already restarted from it before tick() calls resync(). The case the requirement names, contiguous bundles still arriving while ticks stall (a hidden tab), so that only resync() restores the state, is never exercised with a state check.
findings.requirement: a resync from the latest snapshot after a stall or a hidden tab

findings.message: The stable-id de-duplication is tested only for a hit event, at the rollback level (netcode.test.ts:134-147 and 286-299). No test covers a KO event re-simulated by a correction. No test covers the view side: ArenaScene's one-shot flashes keyed by event id (apps/web/src/arenaScene.ts), or DuelClient's pendingEvents buffer, which is capped at 32 (apps/web/src/duelClient.ts:139-144). So nothing shows the view does not show an event twice.
findings.requirement: Events that could repeat after a correction (hits, KO) carry stable ids so the view doesn't show them twice.
